description.invocation: One complete offline image batch inference: infer(model, pixels) = model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode() (resnet_inference.py:14-16), executing the full ResNet-18 FP32 forward on a contiguous CUDA batch of 32 preprocessed NCHW images (the 3 fixture images from pixels.npy cycled via torch.arange(32) % 3, resnet_inference.py:29). Model (FP32, eval, CUDA) and pixels are preloaded before the measured boundary; the call is pure and stateless across repeats.
notes: Measured invocation (user command): python resnet_inference.py --assets /root/autodl-tmp/dev/v6-work/validation-assets/resnet18 --output /tmp/original-resnet, with source defaults --workloads <repo>/workloads.json (common.py:23), --warmup 2, --repeats 5 (common.py:24-25); no --profile.

The repeated unit of work is exactly one infer() call on the offline batch. Statistical warmup/repeats, reference construction and identity replay, negative control, reference tensor saving, profiling and result.json serialization are benchmark-harness infrastructure and must not be inside adapter.run().

Per-repeat measurement protocol (resnet_inference.py:42-48): torch.cuda.synchronize, torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats, time.perf_counter_ns around one infer(), synchronize; samples record latency_ms, images_per_second = batch*1e9/elapsed and peak_allocated_bytes = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(); summarize reports median/min/max.
peak_allocated_bytes is the process-level PyTorch CUDA allocated peak for one forward (reset before each repeat), not whole-device memory, reserved memory or NCCL/driver allocations (README.md).

images_per_second is the source's full-request throughput for the fixed batch of 32 (batch * 1e9 / elapsed around one complete forward on GPU-resident input); it is not a cached-only throughput and must not be converted into one.

Discrete outputs requiring exact comparison: top-1 labels via torch.equal(actual.argmax(-1), reference.argmax(-1)) (resnet_inference.py:33); full 1000-class logits compared with torch.testing.assert_close(atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4) (common.py:74-76); the +1-corruption negative control must be rejected (common.py:79-84).

Precision and numerical policies preserved (common.py:34-42): FP32 weights and activations, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark False, set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.manual_seed(20261020), 4 CPU threads.

Input construction: images = np.load(assets/pixels.npy) to CUDA (verified shape (3,3,224,224) float32); offline batch is images[torch.arange(32, device='cuda') % 3].contiguous() -> (32,3,224,224) FP32, GPU-resident before timing; no H2D transfer or preprocessing inside the measured work.
Model loading is setup outside the measured boundary: ResNetForImageClassification.from_pretrained(args.assets, local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32).cuda().eval() (resnet_inference.py:23).

assumptions: The offline workload row (id=offline, batch=32) is selected per the goal's 'offline image batch inference'; the online batch=1 latency workload executed by the same script run is outside this request.

Reference construction, identity replay, negative control, reference .pt saving, warmup/repeats statistics and optional --profile tracing are measurement infrastructure; the work repeated by adapter.run() is one infer() call on the offline batch.
device_count=1 reflects the workload's single-process CUDA usage (configure(device=0), .cuda()); the second RTX 4090 in the deployment inventory is not required for this workload.

images_per_second keeps the source definition (batch*1e9/elapsed around one complete forward for the fixed batch of 32); the 0.95 baseline ratio from images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio is expressed as a generic ge constraint.
peak_allocated_bytes is the process-level PyTorch CUDA allocated peak measured per repeat after reset_peak_memory_stats; no invented whole-GPU or reserved-memory metric.

The objective is an ordinary evaluator metric; the installed torch_communication collector (NCCL kernel fields) does not apply to this single-GPU task, so no collector source or required_observations are declared.
